title: Presence
description: Connector registration (app.presence topic) and the daemon's view of connectors.

AppPresence.description: Client → daemon. Registers (open: true) or unregisters (open: false) a connector for as long as the bus connection lives; closing the connection unregisters it too. Send again to update.

open.description: false when the app is closing.

context.description: Current app context, e.g. url or project.

home.description: The always-on app that hosts the agent when no other app has it (the overlay). Focus falls back to it.

pid.description: Process that owns the app's windows, so other apps can map a window to it (e.g. the overlay's drop targets).

templates.description: View templates for this app's tool results, keyed by tool name (without the app prefix). Format: protocol/README.md#templates. Kept by the daemon so results still render after the app closes.

components.description: neoui components this app offers the agent, built from the library, keyed by name. The agent writes each as `<app.Name …/>`, the app id, a dot and the name. Format: protocol/README.md#components. Kept by the daemon so docs that use them still draw after the app closes.

description.description: One line for the agent about what the app is for, shown when it first connects in a session. Default: the first sentence of the MCP server's instructions.

AppComponent.description: A neoui component an app offers: what the agent may write as `<app.Name …/>`, and the markup that draws it. The name is a PascalCase identifier; the app id in front makes it its own, so it can clash with no library component and no other app's.

description.description: What it is and when to use it; the agent reads it.

params.description: Its attributes, by name. Each is string, number, boolean or any, optionally an array (string[]) and optionally optional (string?); the optional ones come last.

neoui.description: The body, neoui over the library (not over other app components). The params are in scope by name and as `args`; each use has its own fields, queries and keys.

McpEndpoint.description: The connector's MCP server (Streamable HTTP). The gateway lists its tools and forwards calls to it.

LaunchSpec.description: How to start the app when it is closed (apps_launch). Remembered by the daemon.

command.description: argv; the first entry is the program.

ConnectorInfo.description: A connector the daemon knows, open or not.

v.description: Bumped by the daemon whenever the connector's tool schemas change.

error.description: Why the gateway can't reach its MCP server, if it can't.

home.description: The always-on app that hosts the agent when no other app has it (the overlay). Focus falls back to it.

pid.description: Process that owns the app's windows, so other apps can map a window to it (e.g. the overlay's drop targets).

context.description: The app's current context from its presence.

description.description: One line about what the app is for: its presence's description, else the first sentence of its MCP server's instructions.

skills.description: Its skills, by name and when to load them.

launchable.description: The daemon knows how to start it when it is closed (apps_launch).
